E18.name: What the Long Collapse Sounds Like

E39.name: Becomes a junior scribe. Meets Giana at the scribe shop. Falls in love immediately.

E40.name: Meets Vashten. Close friends within three years. The happiest period of Sero and Giana's lives.

E41.name: Giana falls ill. Sero abandons his post and returns home. Vashten comes and stays with both of them.

E42.name: Second wave of Asharan settlers arrives from Keth. Disease spreads — settlers are immune, have no idea they're carrying it.

E43.name: First witnessed execution. Condemned empire citizens walk willingly to death while Sero pleads. More haunting than if they had resisted.

E44.name: Drought devastates eastern Caldor. Three years. Famine. Refugees flood west.

E45.name: First suspicion he is not aging. Tells himself it's genetics.

E46.name: Confirmation. Twenty years since the ritual. No ambiguity. He says nothing to anyone.

E47.name: Begins ranging across Caldor. Imperial letter of passage. Starts building private records alongside official ones.

E48.name: Empire organizes first large-scale famine relief. Food moves from surplus to starving regions using new roads. It works.

E49.name: Inside the Star-Farers cache: fragmentary references to three other archives on Caldor, Keth, and Mossend. He begins to plan.

E50.name: Caldor declared under imperial governance. Only Caeldrath remains. Empire makes one diplomatic approach. Caeldrath refuses. Empire routes around them.

E51.name: Meets Bard. Roadside inn. Junior scribe who has heard of Sero as legend for 18 months. Shocked by his cynicism.

E52.name: The Century Together. Over 100 years traveling Caldor. Bard gets sick — Vashten arranges partial ritual. Bard survives with extended life.

E53.name: Someone on the road teaches Sero to draw. Early sketches are terrible. Improves over decades.

E54.name: Volcanic eruption west of Caldor. Disrupts harvests for two years.

E55.name: Empire introduces universal currency across Asharan-controlled Caldor.

E56.name: Plague outbreak in imperial capital. Empire's medicine limits casualties. Thousands still die.

E57.name: Empire begins building aqueducts. Water-borne disease drops sharply.

E58.name: Sero refuses another companion. Vashten urges. He refuses.

E59.name: Long solitude begins. Over 250 years largely alone. More efficient, more closed, more precise.

E60.name: Bard dies of old age. Peaceful. Sero writes one entry in the ledger.

E61.name: Northern succession war. Lasts eleven years. Empire mediates badly, installs preferred candidate, creates lasting resentment.

E62.name: Empire establishes formal schools. Literacy begins climbing in major cities.

E63.name: Great storm destroys southern fishing communities. Specific techniques and oral histories lost forever.

E64.name: First Empress transition. The original Empress completes her 250-year reign. Sero is the only person alive who remembers her face when she was young. Does not attend.

E65.name: Sero accidentally discovers abandoned inland trade route. Becomes one of Caldor's busiest roads. No one remembers who found it.

E66.name: Gold discovered in northern mountains. First independent merchant class on Caldor.

E67.name: Famine and fever strike eastern Caldor simultaneously. ~100,000 dead.

E68.name: Vashten dies. Served five Empresses. Final act: appoints Nyneave to find Sero. Last person who knew Sero's original name.

E69.name: Empire commissions continent-wide canal system. Takes 30 years. Outlasts the empire itself.

E70.name: Plague on Keth. Two percent of the home continent dies before containment.

E71.name: Finds Nyneave. Shows her the Renmark archive. Her first question tells him everything. She gets the job.

E72.name: Third Empress takes power. First born after the conquest of Caldor. Has never seen Keth.

E73.name: Great library opens in imperial capital. Sero considers it one of the best things the empire has done.

E74.name: Caldori languages begin dying in major cities. Asharan becomes dominant tongue. Rural areas maintain old languages.

E75.name: Nyneave's aging has visibly slowed. Neither she nor Sero can explain it. She begins documenting it herself.

E76.name: Major earthquake reveals pre-Asharan ruins. Imperial historians rush to claim them. Sero visits before the official excavation.

E77.name: Improved navigation tools. Sea crossing between Caldor and Keth becomes faster.

E78.name: Assassination attempt. Well-organized. Nearly succeeds. Sero survives. Disappears from usual routes for two years.

E79.name: Northern famine. Four years of failed harvests. Worst since the conquest.

E80.name: Returns to find Nyneave has made discoveries he missed in 200 years of working the archive.

E81.name: Caeldrath opens one trade port. First time in 600+ years. Strictly Caeldrath's terms.

E82.name: Nyneave retires. Leaves the archive. Aging accelerates progressively. Dies within months far to the south.

E83.name: The Child Who Asked Too Much. A ten-year-old girl asks Sero questions that stop him cold. Empire kills her as a heretic before he can act.

E84.name: Fourth ruler takes power. Indifference to the people takes time to become apparent.

E85.name: Finds a new vault guardian for the Renmark archive.

E86.name: Fourth ruler's program intensifies. Tax increases. Labor requirements.

E87.name: Slavery formally instituted. Noble class largely collaborates.

E88.name: Underground resistance networks form. Workers, former officials, clergy who refuse to bless slavery.

E89.name: Caeldrath formally denounces the empire. Closes the trade port. Begins accepting Caldori refugees.

E90.name: Armed resistance crushed in three cities simultaneously. Empire creates ten resistors for every one executed.

E91.name: Caldor fractures into 5–6 proto-kingdoms fighting each other.

E92.name: Disease spreads unchecked without the imperial medical system.

E93.name: Famine becomes endemic. Armies burn farmland. Starvation widespread.

E94.name: First journey to Mossend. Third archive found. Months alone. Does not write about this in the ledger.

E95.name: Caeldrath accepts Caldori emigrants. Becomes unintentional repository of Caldori culture.

E96.name: First treaties between successor kingdoms. Frequently violated. Frequently renewed.

E97.name: Caldor's successor kingdoms stabilize. Medieval political landscape. Asharan persists as trade lingua franca.

E98.name: Great interfaith religious council. Produces three new schisms instead of unity.

E99.name: Fifteen-year drought. Collapses two kingdoms. Permanently reshapes Caldor's political map.

E100.name: Navigation breakthrough. Reliable long-distance ocean crossings. Expeditions toward Mossend begin.

E101.name: First permanent settlements on Mossend. Hundreds of years after Sero's first visit.

E102.name: Gunpowder equivalent developed. Transforms warfare within 30 years.

E103.name: New Lands. First contact with a previously unknown civilization. Sero serves as intermediary.

E104.name: Asharan Empire on Keth begins slow decline.

E105.name: Early modern era. The world Sero was born into is unrecognizable.

E106.name: Volcanic event near Mossend. Slows colonization for a generation.

E107.name: Steam power emerges. Sero understands implications completely. Says almost nothing.

E108.name: All three ritual pieces potentially alignable for first time. Sero knows who holds the third element. Begins searching with specific intent.

E109.name: Political movements across Caldor. Literate middle class. Noble structures fracturing.

E110.name: Begins traveling with Boy A and Boy B. Testing through stories in taverns.

E111.name: Boy A dies on the road. Between taverns. Only Sero and Boy B continue.

E112.name: The offer. Boy B hears everything.

E113.name: He keeps moving. The archives and the road. He keeps looking.

events.name: The Ritual
events.whatHappened: Sero is appointed Chief Historian. At a palace ceremony, his blood and the Empress's blood are mixed in a cup by the Shaman. Words are spoken. Sero drinks. Passes out. Wakes 12 hours later confused. His wife thinks it's like being knighted.
events.whyItHappened: The Empress needed someone to serve as the empire's historian and information collector on Caldor — someone who understood both systems. Vashten recommended Sero. The ritual was performed to bind him to the empire permanently.
events.whatItCaused: The foundational event of the entire 2,000-year story. Every subsequent event happens because of this moment.
events.whatWasLearned: Nothing immediately. The implications unfold over decades.
events.draftText:
What nobody tells Sero: That the ritual grants eternal life. That he will never age or get sick. That he can only be killed by physical violence.

Three elements required (learned later): (1) The ruling bloodline of the Asharan Empire. (2) The candidate's blood. (3) A quality possessed by only one specific person in the empire at any time — never Sero, never identified, permanently unexplained.

Permanence: The ritual cannot be transferred to someone else and cannot be prematurely ended. It is fixed to Sero once granted. The only way out is an unnatural death (physical violence).

events.name: The Arrival of the Asharan Empire
events.whatHappened: The Asharan fleet from Keth (L7) makes landfall at Renmark. Twelve local leaders are executed — they were corrupt, extractive, and the empire viewed them as the source of the population's suffering. Fealty is demanded from everyone else.
events.whyItHappened: The Asharan Empire believes it is freeing conquered people from terrible rule, not subjugating them. The conquered are lost subjects who didn't know they belonged.
events.whatItCaused: Sets up every subsequent event. The empire's presence is the condition for everything that follows.
events.whatWasLearned: Systems can genuinely improve things. And good intentions don't make the body count disappear.
events.draftText: Sero's role: Working late when soldiers find him. Captured but unharmed. Over 18 months, proves useful explaining local records. Meets Vashten. Close friends within three years.

events.name: Giana's Death
events.whatHappened: The empire's second wave of civilian settlers from Keth carries a disease Caldori people have no immunity to. The settlers are immune — they don't know they're carrying it. The disease spreads quietly through Renmark, killing roughly a quarter of the city's population. Giana falls ill. Sero abandons his post and comes home. Vashten comes too and stays with both of them. She dies within six months. Last days on the porch watching the ocean. She asks Sero to live a full life.
events.whyItHappened: Not intention. Negligence through ignorance. The empire didn't know. The settlers didn't know. The harm didn't require malice to be devastating.
events.whatItCaused: The emotional root of everything. The standard against which every subsequent relationship and moral decision is measured. His anger at systemic negligence becomes the engine of his early arc.
events.whatWasLearned:
The harm doesn't require intention. Progress has a body count the architects often don't see. And he will not get sick again — though he doesn't yet understand the full shape of what that means.

The full truth comes later (see "The Journal at Vashten's Home" in Events to Be Developed) — Sero doesn't learn he will never age, or the ritual's actual mechanism, until he reads Vashten's own journal at Vashten's home across the ocean.
events.draftText: Sero's response: Not withdrawal. Rage. The empire brought civilization and brought death. He goes to Vashten. Vashten gives him a partial truth, not the full mechanism: he cannot get sick because of the ritual. Vashten frames it mystically — the blood-wine ceremony put something like "god's blood" in him, continuously healing and empowering him. He does not tell Sero that he will never age, or the ritual's actual structure. He does say: "You can't kill your way out of this. And the Empress didn't intend it. But it happened anyway."

events.name: Star-Farers Archive Discovery
events.whatHappened: A local guide mentioned ruins in the interior. Sero investigated. Found a sealed underground chamber containing technology that makes no sense for the era. Documents in an unknown language. Objects he cannot identify. The photograph.
events.whatItCaused: Drives every subsequent archive search. Provides the advanced scientific knowledge (medicine, chemistry, materials) he uses selectively across 2,000 years. Eventually connects to the ritual's origins.
events.whatWasLearned: The empire isn't the apex of civilization. There was something more advanced that disappeared. And inside the cache: fragmentary references to three other archives on Caldor, Keth, and Mossend.
events.draftText:
The photograph: A flat rigid surface bearing a perfect image of people standing before a structure of metal and fire reaching into the sky. He stores it in the archive. Does not carry it. Tells no one.

Why it matters: Proof that an advanced civilization existed before recorded history — and vanished anyway. Knowledge doesn't prevent collapse. The Star-Farers knew things the empire doesn't and they're gone.

events.name: The Drawing Lesson
events.draftText: Someone teaches Sero to draw. Nobody important. That's the point.

events.name: Bard's Trial and Death
events.whatHappened: Bard identified a conspiracy — a coordinated plot against a specific person inside the empire's inner circle. Sero didn't believe him. Bard was right. He exposed the truth in a Socrates-style trial he knew was rigged against him. Used his execution as a platform to speak truth about what the empire was becoming. His final speech spread across civilizations. Sero was with him when he died. Bard looked at him and nodded.
events.whatItCaused: Greatest regret. Shapes every relationship for the next 1,800 years. He preserves everything Bard wrote and calls him a better man than himself.
events.whatWasLearned: He doesn't understand people. His knowledge isolates him from the very thing he needs to understand. Bard was stronger and more principled than him. Being right isn't enough — you have to trust the people around you.
events.draftText: Why Sero didn't believe him: His own certainty. His accumulated knowledge had convinced him he understood the situation better than Bard. He was wrong.

events.name: The Religious War
events.draftText:
Two sects of the same faith war over a doctrinal abstraction. Thousands die. Both sides later revise the very doctrine that caused the war. Sero has the original texts.

Sero's choice: He could end the war with knowledge. He doesn't. People don't change because you give them facts. They change through experience.

What he writes: "I have the truth and I choose silence. The silence is honest. The truth would be arrogance."

events.name: The Minor King
events.draftText:
A good ruler implements genuine reforms. Deposed by nobles. His exact reforms praised as visionary 40 years later under a different ruler.

Sero's prediction: Correct. He knew the king was right and would lose. Was right about both.

What it costs him: Nothing except the knowledge that being right changes nothing.

events.name: First Journey to Keth
events.whatHappened: Sero travels to the empire's homeland for the first time. Finds the deep archives in the Keth imperial capital. Discovers the ritual's full three-element structure. Gets the words of the ceremony. Finds references suggesting the empire knew about the Star-Farers and may have learned the ritual from them.
events.whatItCaused: Gives him the framework for three future ritual attempts. All fail because the third element is never him and never someone he's found at the right moment.
events.draftText:
What he cannot find: The third element. What it is. Who holds it.

What he learned: He's not accidental — he's deliberately made. The ritual is ancient and intentional. And the empire is far older than anyone on Caldor knew. Most importantly: the third element is a person, not a thing (Nyneave's discovery of this detail comes later, ~Age 620).

events.name: The Language That Died
events.draftText: Last native speaker. Sero is the only one left.

events.name: First Caeldrath Denial
events.draftText: Who denies him? Why specifically him?

events.name: The Library Fire
events.draftText:
A private archive of Sero's burned by a panicking local official during a period of civil unrest. He arrives three days too late. Takes inventory of what is gone. Some of it is irreplaceable.

What this breaks: The assumption that obscurity protects knowledge. Distance doesn't protect knowledge. The only thing that protects knowledge is constant vigilance — and he can't be everywhere.

Sero's response: Not nihilism. Anger. He gets to work immediately on distributing and redundancy-building.

events.name: The Collapse
events.whatHappened: The fourth ruler — who had corrupted the empire over 60–70 years through the institution of slavery and extraction — is assassinated by a coalition of nobles, administrators, and resistance leaders. The empire's hold on Caldor ends immediately. No succession plan. No structure to replace it. The institution that organized everything evaporates.
events.whyItHappened: The fourth ruler broke the empire's founding principle — the empire believed it was freeing people, not subjugating them. Once it started subjugating them, the soldiers who were trained in the empire's philosophy of minimal violence refused to enforce it. The administrative class started defecting. The noble class that collaborated became isolated. It fell from the inside.
events.whatItCaused: Everything that follows for the next 300 years.
events.whatWasLearned: He saw this coming decades ago. Knowing something is inevitable doesn't make watching it happen easier. And the empire's best quality — its refusal to become what it opposed — was exactly what prevented it from saving itself.
events.draftText: The empress (at time of collapse): Dead. Killed two days before Sero and Bard arrive in the capital. Not the original Empress — many generations removed. She had tried to force compliance with dwindling authority. Her own soldiers refused. Then she was killed.

events.name: The Underground Evacuation
events.whatHappened: As the city falls, Sero leads a large group of civilians — people from every culture and class, with a handful of former imperial guards — through an ancient tunnel network beneath the city. The tunnels exit northwest, into the hills toward the Mountain People's territory. The worst possible direction. The only option.
events.whatItCaused: The underground city becomes one of the most important civilizations in the post-collapse world. Sero returns across centuries. It becomes the closest thing he has to a permanent home.
events.draftText:
Why Sero knows the tunnels: He was here when they were built. Or before they were abandoned. The tunnels are older than the city above them. The invaders don't know they exist.

The march south: The group emerges from the tunnels and makes for the coast. Camps, fishes, lights fires at night. Former imperial guards who abandoned their posts now protect civilians by default — not by order, just because it's what you do.

The moment everyone looks to Sero: He organized the evacuation. He knew the tunnels. He's calm when no one else is. They treat him as their leader.

Sero tells them he's going back: Waits until the group has structure, guards have organized, the strongest people have stepped up. Then tells them. He's going back to the ruins. There are tens of thousands still there. The knowledge is there. The work is there.

What he learned: People are the archive. The baker who knows how to feed a thousand people. The soldier who knows how to organize a defense. The midwife. The engineer. If the people survive, the knowledge survives. This is the Foundation realization — don't preserve knowledge in one place. Distribute it in people so wide that no single fire can destroy it.

The underground community: Some of the evacuees go back. Some never left the tunnels. The underground city begins forming in the ruins and the tunnels beneath them — beneath the notice of the invaders above. Growing in the dark.

events.name: The Collapse Confrontation
events.draftText: A dying official confronts Sero: "You could have stopped this."

events.name: The Invasion
events.whatHappened: The Mountain People (L10) — a landlocked civilization from the mountainous region west-northwest of the capital — see the power vacuum and move immediately. They've been watching the empire for decades, waiting for this window. The empress is already dead when they arrive. The leaderless soldiers and citizens attempt a defense. It isn't enough.
events.whatItCaused: The ruins become the site of the underground community. The Mountain People's coastal settlement becomes a new power on Caldor. The ruins eventually become something important in their own right.
events.draftText:
What they want: The port. Access to the ocean. Trade routes. Naval capacity. Everything the empire had that a landlocked civilization never could.

What they do to the city: Burn what represents the empire. Preserve the docks, warehouses, and harbor infrastructure. The burning is partly the byproduct of fighting, partly an assertion of dominance. The cultural destruction is real but incidental to their actual goal.

What they build: A coastal garrison around the harbor. A new settlement established slightly along the coast — fresh, away from the ruins, built on their own terms. The ruins of the old city are largely left alone.

Sero's read on The Commander: The most dangerous kind of enemy — one who thinks he's doing the right thing. And who isn't entirely wrong.
events.reviewNote: Wiki-links rewritten: [[Locations#The Mountain People's Homeland|Mountain People]] -> Mountain People (L10)

events.name: The Failed Retirement
events.draftText: Sero tries to stop. Lasts a year. Leaves because he can't not.

events.name: What the Long Collapse Sounds Like
events.draftText: Not plot-driven. Just witnessing.

events.name: First Failed Ritual Attempt
events.whatHappened: For the first time, all pieces seemed alignable. Sero had the words. He believed he had identified the third element. He performed the ceremony. Nothing happened. The third element was absent or wrong.
events.draftText:
Sero's response: One line in his private ledger.

What it cost him: Hope, mostly. He'd been carrying this possibility for centuries.

events.name: The Apathy Years
events.draftText: Sero at his lowest ebb.

events.name: The Plague of Truth
events.draftText: Truth cultists want the archives purged.

events.name: Printing Technology Arrives
events.draftText:
Information can now be duplicated and spread without Sero. His monopoly on knowledge begins to crack. He should feel relieved. He doesn't know what he feels.

Cascade begins: Literacy climbs. Different interpretations spread. Competing narratives emerge. The Religious Council of ~Age 1160 produces three schisms instead of unity — because different printed texts have reached different people.

events.name: The Cartographer's Lie
events.draftText:
A celebrated mapmaker falsifies key geographical details for patrons. Sero has the accurate maps from the Star-Farer archive. Decides not to expose it — doing so would reveal the archive's existence. Stays silent.

What this teaches him: Truth without context is complicated. Sometimes silence is survival. He's not comfortable with this conclusion.

events.name: Second Failed Ritual Attempt
events.whatHappened: Same absence. Sero has become methodical about his failure — treating it as a research problem rather than a hope. Systematic. Almost clinical.
events.draftText: What it cost him: The illusion that this is solvable through effort alone.

events.name: The One Who Lived
events.draftText: A companion who didn't die — just left, lived, thrived.

events.name: The Long Peace
events.draftText:
A region enters 60 years of genuine sustained peace. Sero documents it meticulously. He knows it will end. It ends. War comes from external pressure and internal conflict breaking simultaneously.

What Sero writes: "I knew it would end. I recorded it anyway. Does recording change anything? Or does it just make the ending official?"

events.name: The Successor Who Said No
events.whatHappened: The most serious candidate Sero has ever found. Listens to him for three days. Refuses: "No single person should hold this much continuity. You're asking me to be trapped. And you're wrong about what matters — it's not finding a successor. It's spreading the knowledge out. Teaching. Trusting others."
events.whatItCaused: Everything changes. He is never quite the same kind of seeker again.
events.draftText:
Why she refused: Not fear. Principle. She believed the concentration of knowledge in one person was itself the problem — that Sero had become a hoarding system rather than a teaching one.

Sero's response: He cannot fully refute her. He thinks about what she said for the next 100+ years.

What it cost him: His framework. The 1,350-year goal is suddenly questionable.

What it gave him: The seed of the Foundation realization that will bloom fully after the collapse — which happened 500 years earlier in the timeline. (Note: In Sero's internal arc, the collapse ~Age 820 gives him the Foundation insight through experience. The Successor Who Said No gives him the philosophical language for it ~Age 1350. Both are necessary.)

events.name: Third Visit to Keth
events.draftText: The empire's decline. Someone asks a question he cannot answer.

events.name: Third Failed Ritual Attempt
events.whatHappened: Third attempt. Still nothing. But this time something shifts in how he thinks about the problem — he begins wondering whether the candidate and the third-element person might be found through the same search. That the right candidate might be the third element.
events.draftText: What it cost him: 500 years of searching. He's still no closer to a solution, but the framework finally changes.

events.name: Early Newspapers
events.draftText: Information moves faster than Sero can verify it. People react to news that may or may not be accurate. He's no longer the primary conduit for anything. Just one voice among many — and not even a loud one.

events.name: The Invention He Recognized
events.draftText: A new technology emerges that Sero recognizes from the Star-Farer archive. He watches its development with dread. He knows exactly where this leads — he has the documentation. He says almost nothing to almost anyone.

events.name: The Technology Collapse
events.whatItCaused: A cautionary pattern he recognizes in every subsequent technological development.
events.draftText:
A landlocked kingdom (ironic echo of the Mountain People) adopts the new productive technology completely. Builds everything around it. Assumes infinite growth. Resources deplete. Soil exhausts. Waters become unusable. The kingdom doubles down — pushes the technology harder. Famine. Migration. Instability. Collapse over decades.

Sero documents it: Every stage. How one innovation broke a society. He writes: "The Star-Farers probably knew this too. I wonder if that's why they left."

events.name: The Wrong History Book
events.draftText:
The standard history of the Long Collapse is published. Almost entirely wrong about its causes. Sero has every record the historian didn't have.

The decision: Does he reach out? Does he correct the record? He considers it. Changes his mind. Changes it back. Ultimately chooses — and the choice itself is the story.

events.name: Before the Two Boys
events.draftText: 80 years of failed candidates before he finds them.

events.name: The Final Refusal
events.whatHappened: Boy B hears the full story. Is offered the role. Refuses: "I will carry your stories as far as an ordinary life allows, and I will tell people the truth where I can. But I cannot be what you are. The loneliness would destroy me."
events.whatItCaused: He keeps moving. The archives and the road. He keeps looking — maybe not for a successor anymore. Maybe just to see what happens next.
events.whatWasLearned: The burden doesn't transfer. And that might be correct. Boy B's refusal isn't failure — it's the answer the Successor Who Said No was pointing toward 600 years ago. The knowledge lives in everyone who carries a piece of it. Not in one person.
events.draftText: Sero's response: "That's the right answer."

events.draftText: See Political List — running document.

events.name: The Journal at Vashten's Home
events.draftText: Happens sometime after Giana's Death (Age 23), likely before Vashten's death (~Age 350–400). Sero and Vashten travel across the ocean to Vashten's home. Sero reads Vashten's own journal and learns the full truth: the ritual is why he never ages and heals quickly, not just why he can't get sick. Needs an exact Age and to be reconciled against the "First Journey to Keth" event (~Age 380, currently listed as Sero alone) — may be the same trip or a separate, earlier one.

events.draftText: See Descendants List — running document.

events.name: Becomes a junior scribe. Meets Giana at the scribe shop. Falls in love immediately.
events.whatHappened: Sero takes a job at the scribe shop. It's a shop that is run by the nobility. When they have letters to be written or contracts for business or whatever nonsense they may need, these are the record keepers of the kingdom.

events.name: Meets Vashten. Close friends within three years. The happiest period of Sero and Giana's lives.
Giana falls ill. Sero abandons his post and returns home. Vashten comes and stays with both of them.
Second wave of Asharan settlers arrives from Keth. Disease spreads — settlers are immune, have no idea they're carrying it.
First witnessed execution. Condemned empire citizens walk willingly to death while Sero pleads. More haunting than if they had resisted.
Drought devastates eastern Caldor. Three years. Famine. Refugees flood west.
First suspicion he is not aging. Tells himself it's genetics.
Confirmation. Twenty years since the ritual. No ambiguity. He says nothing to anyone.
Begins ranging across Caldor. Imperial letter of passage. Starts building private records alongside official ones.
Empire organizes first large-scale famine relief. Food moves from surplus to starving regions using new roads. It works.
Inside the Star-Farers cache: fragmentary references to three other archives on Caldor, Keth, and Mossend. He begins to plan.
Caldor declared under imperial governance. Only Caeldrath remains. Empire makes one diplomatic approach. Caeldrath refuses. Empire routes around them.
Meets Bard. Roadside inn. Junior scribe who has heard of Sero as legend for 18 months. Shocked by his cynicism.
The Century Together. Over 100 years traveling Caldor. Bard gets sick — Vashten arranges partial ritual. Bard survives with extended life.
Someone on the road teaches Sero to draw. Early sketches are terrible. Improves over decades.
Volcanic eruption west of Caldor. Disrupts harvests for two years.
Empire introduces universal currency across Asharan-controlled Caldor.
Plague outbreak in imperial capital. Empire's medicine limits casualties. Thousands still die.
Empire begins building aqueducts. Water-borne disease drops sharply.
Sero refuses another companion. Vashten urges. He refuses.
Long solitude begins. Over 250 years largely alone. More efficient, more closed, more precise.
Bard dies of old age. Peaceful. Sero writes one entry in the ledger.
Northern succession war. Lasts eleven years. Empire mediates badly, installs preferred candidate, creates lasting resentment.
Empire establishes formal schools. Literacy begins climbing in major cities.
Great storm destroys southern fishing communities. Specific techniques and oral histories lost forever.
First Empress transition. The original Empress completes her 250-year reign. Sero is the only person alive who remembers her face when she was young. Does not attend.
Sero accidentally discovers abandoned inland trade route. Becomes one of Caldor's busiest roads. No one remembers who found it.
Gold discovered in northern mountains. First independent merchant class on Caldor.
Famine and fever strike eastern Caldor simultaneously. ~100,000 dead.
Vashten dies. Served five Empresses. Final act: appoints Nyneave to find Sero. Last person who knew Sero's original name.
Empire commissions continent-wide canal system. Takes 30 years. Outlasts the empire itself.
Plague on Keth. Two percent of the home continent dies before containment.
Finds Nyneave. Shows her the Renmark archive. Her first question tells him everything. She gets the job.
Third Empress takes power. First born after the conquest of Caldor. Has never seen Keth.
Great library opens in imperial capital. Sero considers it one of the best things the empire has done.
Caldori languages begin dying in major cities. Asharan becomes dominant tongue. Rural areas maintain old languages.
Nyneave's aging has visibly slowed. Neither she nor Sero can explain it. She begins documenting it herself.
Major earthquake reveals pre-Asharan ruins. Imperial historians rush to claim them. Sero visits before the official excavation.
Improved navigation tools. Sea crossing between Caldor and Keth becomes faster.
Assassination attempt. Well-organized. Nearly succeeds. Sero survives. Disappears from usual routes for two years.
Northern famine. Four years of failed harvests. Worst since the conquest.
Returns to find Nyneave has made discoveries he missed in 200 years of working the archive.
Caeldrath opens one trade port. First time in 600+ years. Strictly Caeldrath's terms.
Nyneave retires. Leaves the archive. Aging accelerates progressively. Dies within months far to the south.
The Child Who Asked Too Much. A ten-year-old girl asks Sero questions that stop him cold. Empire kills her as a heretic before he can act.
Fourth ruler takes power. Indifference to the people takes time to become apparent.
Finds a new vault guardian for the Renmark archive.
Fourth ruler's program intensifies. Tax increases. Labor requirements.
Slavery formally instituted. Noble class largely collaborates.
Underground resistance networks form. Workers, former officials, clergy who refuse to bless slavery.
Caeldrath formally denounces the empire. Closes the trade port. Begins accepting Caldori refugees.
Armed resistance crushed in three cities simultaneously. Empire creates ten resistors for every one executed.
Caldor fractures into 5–6 proto-kingdoms fighting each other.
Disease spreads unchecked without the imperial medical system.
Famine becomes endemic. Armies burn farmland. Starvation widespread.
First journey to Mossend. Third archive found. Months alone. Does not write about this in the ledger.
Caeldrath accepts Caldori emigrants. Becomes unintentional repository of Caldori culture.
First treaties between successor kingdoms. Frequently violated. Frequently renewed.
Caldor's successor kingdoms stabilize. Medieval political landscape. Asharan persists as trade lingua franca.
Great interfaith religious council. Produces three new schisms instead of unity.
Fifteen-year drought. Collapses two kingdoms. Permanently reshapes Caldor's political map.
Navigation breakthrough. Reliable long-distance ocean crossings. Expeditions toward Mossend begin.
First permanent settlements on Mossend. Hundreds of years after Sero's first visit.
Gunpowder equivalent developed. Transforms warfare within 30 years.
New Lands. First contact with a previously unknown civilization. Sero serves as intermediary.
Asharan Empire on Keth begins slow decline.
Early modern era. The world Sero was born into is unrecognizable.
Volcanic event near Mossend. Slows colonization for a generation.
Steam power emerges. Sero understands implications completely. Says almost nothing.
All three ritual pieces potentially alignable for first time. Sero knows who holds the third element. Begins searching with specific intent.
Political movements across Caldor. Literate middle class. Noble structures fracturing.
Begins traveling with Boy A and Boy B. Testing through stories in taverns.
Boy A dies on the road. Between taverns. Only Sero and Boy B continue.
The offer. Boy B hears everything.
He keeps moving. The archives and the road. He keeps looking.
